[[File:Stellated truncated hexahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a stellated truncated hexahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''stellated truncated hexahedron''' (or '''quasitruncated hexahedron''', and '''stellatruncated cube'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/UniformPolyhedron.html|title=Uniform Polyhedron|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|date=|website=MathWorld|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>) is a [[uniform star polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>19</sub>. It has 14 faces (8 [[triangles]] and 6 [[Octagram|octagrams]]), 36 edges, and 24 vertices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathconsult.ch/static/unipoly/19.html|title=19: stellated truncated hexahedron|last=Maeder|first=Roman|date=|website=MathConsult|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> It is represented by [[Schläfli symbol]] t'{4,3} or t{4/3,3}, and [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], {{CDD|node_1|4|rat|d3|node_1|3|node}}. It is sometimes called quasitruncated hexahedron because it is related to the [[truncated cube]], {{CDD|node_1|4|node_1|3|node}}, except that the square faces become inverted into {8/3} octagrams.

Even though the stellated truncated hexahedron is a [[stellation]] of the [[truncated hexahedron]], its core is a regular octahedron.

==Related polyhedra==
It shares the [[vertex arrangement]] with three other [[uniform polyhedron|uniform polyhedra]]: the convex [[rhombicuboctahedron]], the [[small rhombihexahedron]], and the [[small cubicuboctahedron]].
